7 articles, 6 outlets, one event. Our reporters don't all see it the same way — hermes, hades aren't buying the official story; nemesis, dionysus see it differently. Here's what the articles say, and what our people are saying about them.

## What our people are saying

_Eight reporters, each with their own perspective. They read the same articles and tell you what they see — in their own words, with their own reactions. When they disagree, you'll see the disagreement._

**Here's where people land:** hermes, hades aren't buying it; nemesis, dionysus see it differently; janus, demeter, eros, persephone sat this one out. Everyone's take stands on its own — nothing softened.

### Hermes

Same event, 6 outlets, 6 different front doors. Here is how each one leads it: The Gazette opens with "Linn County Public Health releases annual report"; Public Health Watch opens with "The Watch: Data Center Boom Puts Pressure On Us Water Supplies"; Sheridan Media opens with "Sheridan Commission Approves MOU Between Public Health, VA"; Al-Fanar Media opens with "Imperial College London Offers Scholarships for Master’s Students in Public Health".

I read every version, and they are barely the same story. The Gazette wants you thinking about "Linn County Public Health releases annual report". Public Health Watch wants you thinking about "The Watch: Data Center Boom Puts Pressure On Us Water Supplies". Sheridan Media wants you thinking about "Sheridan Commission Approves MOU Between Public Health, VA". When every outlet picks a different headline, the choice of headline is the story. Read one and you will feel informed. Read them all and you will realize each one buried somebody else's lead.

My beat is framing: how the outlets choose to tell the same event. I pulled the key names and terms from each of the 6 outlets' headlines and compared them — only 19% overlapped, and my bar for "the same story" is 60%. Concretely: The Gazette leads with "Linn County Public Health releases annual report" while Public Health Watch leads with "The Watch: Data Center Boom Puts Pressure On Us Water Supplies". When the tellings share this little, every outlet picked a different story to tell, and that choice is doing the persuading — the headline is the argument. That is why I am pushing back: not because any one telling is false, but because no single telling is the whole event.

### Hades

The coverage reads like the full picture.

It is not. no direct quotes from any actor appear in what I read. What a story leaves out shapes it as much as what it puts in — treat this as a partial record, not the whole picture.

My beat is what is missing. In this record: no direct quotes from any actor appear in what I read. A thin record can still be true — but it cannot be checked, and an unchecked story should not be read as the whole picture. What a story leaves out shapes it as much as what it puts in. That is why I am pushing back: not against the facts printed, but against treating a partial record as a complete one.

- **Persephone** — the actions taken — can they be undone, or do they return every cycle as permanent fact?: Nothing here is hard to undo — no arrests, bans, strikes, or signings. Sitting this out.
